title: Monarch Spin Plasmid Miniprep (NEB)
author: Owen Butler
materials: Discard the supernatant into a 10% bleach solution.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace
steps.instruction: Clean the work area and prepare equipment to prevent contamination.

substeps.instruction: Wipe benches and pipettes with DNA-Away, then RNAse-Away, and finally with 70% ethanol.
Light the bunsen burner and work closely to it during the Validation of Overnight Culture steps.

steps.title: Prepare Elution Buffer
steps.instruction: Pre-heat Elution Buffer or NFW to 50 °C in a bead-bath or incubator for later use.

steps.title: Resuspend Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 200 µL of Buffer B1.

substeps.instruction: Gently pipette to mix.
Transfer the suspension to a pre-labeled 1.5 mL eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of Buffer B2 to the tube.

substeps.instruction: Gently invert the tube 10 times (do not vortex).
Incubate at room temperature for 00:01:00. The solution should become transparent, viscous, and dark pink.
Do not incubate longer than 1 minute to prevent irreversible plasmid denaturation.

steps.title: Neutralize Lysate
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of Buffer B3 to the tube.

substeps.instruction: Gently invert the tube until neutralized (color should be uniformly yellow).
Incubate at room temperature for 00:02:00.

steps.title: Clear Lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 16000 x g for 5 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Verify that the pellet is compact and adhered to the side of the tube.
If the pellet is not strongly adhered, spin again at 16000 x g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Column
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to the spin column and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Tilt the eppendorf tube away from the pellet and carefully pipette up the supernatant, ensuring the tip does not touch the pellet or debris.
Transfer 800 µL of supernatant to the spin column.
Centrifuge at 16000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: Wash Column with Buffer BZ
steps.instruction: Wash the column using Buffer BZ.

substeps.instruction: Re-insert the column into the same collection tube.
Add 200 µL of Buffer BZ.
Centrifuge at 16000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: Wash Column with Buffer WZ
steps.instruction: Wash the column using Buffer WZ.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL of Buffer WZ.
Centrifuge at 16000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: Dry Column
steps.instruction: Remove residual ethanol from the column.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the column to a clean, pre-labeled 1.5 mL eppendorf tube, ensuring the tip does not touch the flow-through in the collection tube.
With the snap-cap open, let ethanol evaporate for 00:02:00 while the column sits in the 1.5 mL eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Elute the plasmid DNA from the column matrix.

substeps.instruction: Add 45 µL of pre-heated (50 °C) Elution Buffer or NFW to the center of the column's matrix.
Incubate for 00:05:00 at 37 °C.
Spin at 16000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: Maximize DNA Yield
steps.instruction: Perform a second elution pass to increase yield.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the flow-through from the 1.5 mL eppendorf tube back into the column's matrix.
Incubate for 00:03:00 at 37 °C.
Spin at 16000 x g for 1 minute.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Store the eluted DNA based on the required duration.

substeps.instruction: For short-term storage, store at 4 °C.
For long-term storage (> 1 day), store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Clean Up and Waste Disposal
steps.instruction: Dispose of all waste and clean the station.

substeps.instruction: Discard flow-through in the collection tube into the 'Ethanol waste' beaker.
Dab the bottom of the collection tube on a KimWipe to absorb excess flow-through.
Empty the ethanol beaker into the ethanol waste collection site.
Add 10% bleach solution to remaining overnight cultures, wait 00:30:00, then pour down the drain with water.
Dispose of culture tubes in biohazard.

description: Obtain a clear round-bottom 96w plate. Download the attached excel sheet. Record the specific plate map that will be used for each run on the excel sheet. OD600_analysis.xlsx The plate map below is an example for 2 samples. BLANK BLANK SAMPLE 1 SAMPLE 1 SAMPLE 2 SAMPLE 2 OD600 Measurement of Overnight Cultures Save and file the excel sheet in the appropriate location. In the clear round-bottom 96w plate, add 100 µL of the appropriate media in duplicate in the designated wells from the plate map above. These are the BLANKS. The blanks are used to account for the background absorbance due to the media in which the cells are grown. If the cultures are sufficiently grown (OD corrected > 1), proceed. Extinguish the bunsen burner. Once finished reading, add 10% bleach to each sample well of the 96w plate. After 10 minutes, empty the plate down the drain with water. Discard the plate in a biohazard box. Nanodrop Refer to the NanoDrop Protocol . In the clear round-bottom 96w plate, add 90 µL of appropriate media and 10 µL of each overnight culture (pipette to mix before transferring culture) in duplicate into the designated wells, to make 1:10 dilutions. Ensure to mix the wells thoroughly once added. Save overnight cultures for the following steps. Read OD600 using the BioTek Synergy H1 microplate reader. Copy the blanks and the OD values into the excel sheet downloaded in a previous step. The sheet will perform the following calculations to correct the sample measurements. OD corrected = (OD sample − average (OD blanks ) ) * 10
